blocking.where: history.mdx — 'What This Adds Up To' section
blocking.claim: "A funded, ambitious public plan for the whole waterfront stalled with no confirmed outcome, while a storm-damaged boardwalk sat broken for over a year."
blocking.problem: Calls the Lake Ontario Park master plan "funded" and headlines the section above it "A Master Plan That Never Got Built" — both directly contradict the page's own earlier, correctly-hedged statement two paragraphs prior in the same file: "No source available for this page confirms the promenade, or the wider master plan, was ever funded or built." A reader hits three different certainty levels (unfunded/unbuilt is unconfirmed; then flatly 'never got built'; then flatly 'funded') for the same fact in one article.
blocking.evidence: F18/F19 (Star 2010): plan was 'prepared for Waterfront Toronto in 2008' with an estimated ~$17M promenade cost; sheet dead_ends: 'No confirmation of whether the 2008 Lake Ontario Park master plan or its $17M promenade was ever funded or built.'
blocking.fix: Replace "A funded, ambitious public plan for the whole waterfront stalled with no confirmed outcome" with "An ambitious public plan for the whole waterfront, of unconfirmed funding, stalled with no confirmed outcome". Also change the section header "A Master Plan That Never Got Built" to "A Master Plan With No Confirmed Outcome" so it no longer asserts certainty the sourcing doesn't support.

blocking.where: history.mdx — 'One Family, One Contract, Two Decades Renewed' section
blocking.claim: "No source in the research for this page confirms whether the Foulidis concession or the Boardwalk Pub is still the operating arrangement today..."
blocking.problem: This hedge lumps together two different things: whether the specific restaurant (Boardwalk Pub) still operates, and whether the legal concession (the Foulidis family's exclusive rights) is still in force. The second is knowable from public record independent of the Star's 2010 field visit — council's 2007 vote renewed it for 20 more years, i.e. through 2027, which is still in effect as of this page's research date (2026-09-13). By extending the hedge to the concession itself, the sentence directly undercuts the spike_statement, subtitle, and reckoning_pullquote, which all assert in confident present tense that one family currently holds the concession ('for two decades and counting', 'renewed by council for 20 more'). The page can't simultaneously headline this as a live, ongoing arrangement and then tell the reader in the body that nobody knows if it's still the arrangement.
blocking.evidence: F11 (derivation D01): 2007 council vote renewed the concession without competitive bid for 20 more years, i.e. through 2027. Subtitle: 'one family has held for two decades and counting.' Spike: 'renewed by council for 20 more.'
blocking.fix: Replace the sentence with: "No source in the research for this page confirms whether the Boardwalk Pub specifically is still open today; the concession itself, per the 2007 council vote, runs through 2027. The sourced pricing and vendor details here are pinned to 2010."

advisory.where: showcase.json subtitle / spike_statement ('two decades and counting' / '20+ years')
advisory.claim: "one family has held for two decades and counting"
advisory.problem: The sheet doesn't pin an exact start year for the concession, only that it had run 20 years as of the 2010 Star profile and was then renewed in 2007 for 20 more (through 2027). Depending on which span 'two decades and counting' is meant to describe, the family's total tenure by 2026 could read as anywhere from ~19 years (counting the 2007 renewal term) to ~36+ years (counting from the original start implied by the 2010 'held for 20 years' line). The page never clarifies which span it means, leaving the headline number ambiguous rather than clearly wrong.
advisory.evidence: F11: "...have been held by george foulidis and his family for 20 years. three years ago bussin spearheaded a successful vote at city council to renew it without competitive bids for 20 more years."
advisory.fix: Consider anchoring the subtitle to the sourced renewal date explicitly, e.g. "...run under a food-and-alcohol concession renewed by city council in 2007 for 20 years, without a competitive bid," which avoids the ambiguous running total.
